newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares break record run in profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares break record run in profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-taking on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday reversed a rising trend which had pushed Hungarian shares to seven successive daily records.
"Everybody had expected a technical correction, they just did not know when it would come," said Rudi Voros, London-based analyst of ICE Securities. "What we are speaking about is profit-taking."
The BUX index finished at 6,292.91 points, down 70.02 points or 1.11 percent.
Traders said a fall of Hungarian shares on London's SEAQ set the tone for the Budapest bourse.
The BUX opened some 40 points down and it bottomed at levels about 90 points below Monday's closing levels, but a recovering buying side helped it rise again shortly before the closing, traders said.

They added that Hungarian and foreign investors were mainly sellers, but at the lower price levels buyers appeared quickly and the spot share turnover of the BSE rose to 3.99 billion forints from Monday's 2.18 billion forints.
Attila Gazdik of New York Broker said that further downward corrections may come, but he was optimistic as he saw strong support for the price of several heavyweight shares.
"I think there is still strength in the market, and I see a chance for further price rises," he said.
"I do not feel a real selling wave," he said, adding that news about Hungary's economic performance was good.
Voros agreed that prices may continue to drop slightly, but he added the market was likely to stagnate in the next few weeks until the release of first half corporate results.
He said the BSE was boosted by funds directed to Hungary from the Czech Republic recently, while the Cezch government fought for stabilising the crown.

"But this process seems to have ceased," he said, adding that Czech stocks firmed on Tuesday and turnover on the Czech bourse was substantial on Monday, while it was low on the Budapest Stock Exchange.
